The pipeline uses Bash, CDO and Python, so it runs in a **Linux shell**. On Windows that shell is
**WSL2 (Ubuntu)**; on macOS and Linux it is your normal terminal. Pick your system once — the tabs on
this page stay in sync.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Before you start
- ~5 GB free disk (one month of raw METREF disk files is ~1–2 GB).
- An **LSA SAF account** (free) — registration can take a while to be activated, so do step 6 first if you have not registered yet.
- Admin rights on Windows for installing WSL (once).
:::

## 1 · Get a Linux terminal {#terminal}

::: {.panel-tabset group="os"}

## Windows (WSL2)

::: {.steps}
::: {.step}
**Install WSL2 + Ubuntu (once).** Start menu → type **PowerShell** → right-click → **Run as administrator**:

```powershell
wsl --install -d Ubuntu
```

Restart Windows when asked. If the command prints help text instead of installing, run
`wsl --list --online` and then `wsl --install -d Ubuntu` again.
:::

::: {.step}
**First launch.** Open **Ubuntu** from the Start menu and wait for the initialisation. Choose a Linux
username and password (the password is not echoed while you type — that is normal).
:::

::: {.step}
**Check it is WSL 2.** In PowerShell:

```powershell
wsl --list --verbose          # Ubuntu ... VERSION 2
wsl --set-version Ubuntu 2    # only if it shows VERSION 1
```
:::

::: {.step}
**Open WSL every time you work on the tutorial** — any of these gives you the same Ubuntu shell:

- Start menu → **Ubuntu**, or
- **Windows Terminal** → ⌄ dropdown → **Ubuntu**, or
- type `wsl` in PowerShell / `cmd`, then `cd ~`.

Your prompt now looks like `yourname@PC:~$`. Everything below runs **in this window**.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Work inside the Linux file system
Keep the project under `~/` (e.g. `~/projects/tutorial-repo`), **not** under `/mnt/c/...`.
Windows drives mounted in WSL are 5–10× slower for thousands of small files (raw NetCDF, Zarr chunks).
To see the files from Windows, run `explorer.exe .` inside the folder or open
`\\wsl$\Ubuntu\home\<you>\projects` in File Explorer.
:::

Official guide: <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install>

## macOS

Open **Terminal** (⌘ + Space → "Terminal"). Install [Homebrew](https://brew.sh) if you do not have it.

## Linux

Open your terminal (Ubuntu/Debian: `Ctrl + Alt + T`). Commands below use `apt`; use your distribution's
package manager otherwise.

:::

## 2 · Install system tools {#tools}

::: {.panel-tabset group="os"}

## Windows (WSL2)

In the **Ubuntu** window:

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y git wget curl ca-certificates cdo
```

## macOS

```bash
brew install git wget cdo
```

## Linux

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y git wget curl ca-certificates cdo
```

:::

Then install **uv**, the Python package and environment manager used by this project
(it also downloads the right Python version for you):

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
source "$HOME/.local/bin/env"      # or open a new terminal
```

Check everything in one go:

::: {.terminal}
```bash
git --version && wget --version | head -n1 && cdo -V 2>&1 | head -n1 && uv --version
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## CDO is not a Python package
`pip`/`uv` cannot install CDO. If `apt`/`brew` is not an option, use a conda-forge environment:
`conda install -c conda-forge cdo` and make sure `cdo` is on your `PATH`.
:::

## 3 · Clone the repository {#clone}

```bash
mkdir -p ~/projects && cd ~/projects
git clone https://github.com/khizerzakir/tutorial-repo.git
cd tutorial-repo
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**All commands in this tutorial run from the repository root** (`~/projects/tutorial-repo`).
If you get lost: `cd ~/projects/tutorial-repo`. Already cloned earlier? Update with `git pull`.
:::

## 4 · Create the Python environment {#python}

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra notebook                                         # <1>
uv run python -c "import xarray, zarr; print('xarray', xarray.__version__, '| zarr', zarr.__version__)"  # <2>
```
1. Creates `.venv/` with the exact versions from `uv.lock`, including JupyterLab for the notebooks.
2. Must print **zarr 3.x**. The cube builder refuses to run with Zarr 2.

::: {.callout-important}
## Always run project commands through `uv run`
`02_preprocess_cdo.sh` calls `python3` internally (YAML + grid helper). Starting it as
`uv run bash code/02_preprocess_cdo.sh …` puts the project environment first on `PATH`, so those
imports work. Alternatively activate the environment once per terminal: `source .venv/bin/activate`.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Prefer plain pip?
```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt jupyterlab
```
Python ≥ 3.12 is required (Ubuntu 24.04 ships 3.12; on 22.04 use uv). Never use `sudo pip`.
In this mode drop the `uv run` prefix from the commands in this tutorial.
:::

## 5 · Open the project in VS Code (optional, recommended) {#vscode}

::: {.panel-tabset group="os"}

## Windows (WSL2)

1. Install [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/download) **on Windows** (not inside Ubuntu).
2. Extensions (`Ctrl+Shift+X`): **WSL**, **Python**, **Jupyter** (all by Microsoft).
3. In the Ubuntu window, from the repository root:

   ```bash
   code .
   ```

   The first run installs the VS Code server inside WSL. The bottom-left corner must show
   **WSL: Ubuntu**. Open a terminal inside VS Code with ``Ctrl+` `` — it is already in the repository root.
4. When you open a notebook, pick the kernel **`.venv/bin/python`** (top-right "Select Kernel").

Guide: <https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/remote/wsl>

## macOS

Install [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/download) with the **Python** and **Jupyter**
extensions, then from the repository root run `code .` (enable it via *Command Palette → Shell Command:
Install 'code' command in PATH*). Select the **`.venv/bin/python`** kernel for notebooks.

## Linux

Install [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/download) with the **Python** and **Jupyter**
extensions and run `code .` from the repository root. Select the **`.venv/bin/python`** kernel for notebooks.

:::

## 6 · LSA SAF credentials {#credentials}

::: {.steps}
::: {.step}
Register on the [LSA SAF Data Service](https://datalsasaf.lsasvcs.ipma.pt/) and activate your account.

![Data portal registration](imgs/portal_reg.png){width="85%"}
:::

::: {.step}
Create your private settings file and open it:

```bash
cp code/.env.example code/.env
nano code/.env          # or: code code/.env
```
:::

::: {.step}
Fill in your account and the product you want. The download script reads exactly these names:

```dotenv
LSASAF_USERNAME="your_username"
LSASAF_PASSWORD="your_password"
SAMPLE_YEAR=2015
SAMPLE_MONTH=06
VARIABLE_NAME=METREF
URL="https://datalsasaf.lsasvcs.ipma.pt/PRODUCTS/MSG/METREF/NETCDF"
```

`code/.env` is listed in `.gitignore` — never commit it, never paste it in screenshots or chats.
:::

::: {.step}
Browse the product folders to confirm the URL and that your month exists:

- [METREF — reference evapotranspiration](https://datalsasaf.lsasvcs.ipma.pt/PRODUCTS/MSG/METREF/)
- [MDFVC — fractional vegetation cover](https://datalsasaf.lsasvcs.ipma.pt/PRODUCTS/MSG/MDFVC/)

![Browse the products](imgs/browse.png){width="85%"}
:::
:::

## ✅ Setup checklist {#checklist}

- [ ] A Linux shell is open (Ubuntu/WSL on Windows) and `pwd` ends in `/tutorial-repo`
- [ ] `cdo -V`, `wget --version`, `git --version`, `uv --version` all work
- [ ] `uv run python -c "import zarr; print(zarr.__version__)"` prints 3.x
- [ ] `code/.env` exists with your username, password and product `URL`
